purpose: Move beyond linear syndrome compression with an exact graph-changing contraction on maximum-degree-four 3-colourability cores. After degree<=2 peeling, delete every connected component of current degree-three vertices that is not a Gallai tree. Any colouring of the remaining graph extends across such a component by the Borodin--Erdos--Rubin--Taylor degree-choosability theorem, and the extension can be reconstructed in polynomial time.

input_regime.graph: A simple graph G with maximum degree at most four, as in the NP-hard max-degree-four / 4-regular 3-COLOR source frontier.
input_regime.preprocess: First exhaust the exact v5.0 degree<=2 peel. Thus every remaining vertex has degree three or four unless a K4/subcubic terminal has already fired.
input_regime.degree3_layer: Let S={v:deg_G(v)=3}. Consider a connected component H of the induced subgraph G[S].

boundary_list_lemma.outside_colouring: Fix any proper 3-colouring phi of G-V(H).
boundary_list_lemma.available_list: For v in H let L(v) be the three colours minus the colours used by neighbours of v outside H.
boundary_list_lemma.count: Because v has total degree three and every degree-three neighbour belongs to the same S-component H, the number of outside neighbours is exactly 3-d_H(v). Therefore |L(v)|>=3-(3-d_H(v))=d_H(v).
boundary_list_lemma.meaning: Extending phi to H is a degree-list-colouring problem on H.

degree_choosability_theorem.source_fact: Borodin and independently Erdos--Rubin--Taylor characterize connected degree-choosable graphs: H is colourable from every list assignment with |L(v)|>=d_H(v) iff H is not a Gallai tree.
degree_choosability_theorem.Gallai_tree: A connected graph whose every block is a complete graph or an odd cycle.
degree_choosability_theorem.extension: If H is not a Gallai tree, the boundary lists above always admit a proper L-colouring. Thus every proper 3-colouring of G-H extends to G.
degree_choosability_theorem.equivalence: Consequently G is 3-colourable iff G-H is 3-colourable whenever H is a non-Gallai component of the current degree-three layer.

loop: Exhaust degree<=2 peeling, storing deleted vertices and their then-current neighbour lists for reverse reconstruction.
Compute connected components of the current degree-three induced subgraph.
Recognize Gallai trees by block decomposition: every block must be a clique or an odd cycle.
If a non-Gallai component H exists, delete all vertices of H and store H together with its outside-neighbour incidences; then restart low-degree peeling because boundary degrees may have fallen.
Stop when neither low-degree peeling nor non-Gallai degree-three deletion applies.
kernel_algorithm.progress: Every substantive step deletes at least one vertex. Block decomposition, degree updates and degree-list colouring are polynomial; a straightforward implementation is polynomial even without dynamic optimization.
reconstruction: Undo stored deletions in reverse order.

For a deleted non-Gallai H, all vertices that were outside H at deletion time are already coloured. Build the boundary lists L(v) and run a constructive degree-list-colouring algorithm guaranteed by the theorem.
For degree<=2 peeled vertices, use the v5.0 greedy reverse insertion rule.

terminal_normal_form.statement: At a nonterminal fixed point, minimum degree is at least three and every connected component of the degree-three induced subgraph is a Gallai tree.
terminal_normal_form.max_degree_four_shape: Hence the residual consists of degree-four vertices coupled through degree-three Gallai-tree pieces whose blocks are only K2/K3/K4 or odd cycles (subject to the ambient degree-three bound).
terminal_normal_form.K4_note: A degree-three component equal to K4 is itself an explicit non-3-colourable component and should be rejected immediately rather than retained as a boundary gadget.

source_return_firewall.four_regular: On a 4-regular input S is empty, so the contraction deletes nothing. Since 3-COLOR is NP-complete on 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs, this preprocessing theorem is not a universal solver.
source_return_firewall.odd_wheels: Odd wheels contain a high-degree hub and are outside the max-degree-four family once the rim length exceeds four; v6.3 remains a syndrome-compression barrier, not a counterexample to this graph reduction.
source_return_firewall.meaning: The contraction is genuine exact progress on mixed degree-3/4 instances while preserving a clean NP-hard source-return class on which it is silent.

positive: A new deterministic polynomial exact contraction independent of linear syndrome hashing, Polynomial Calculus and autarky cones.
Polynomial witness lifting follows from list colouring, not from branching over boundary colour assignments.
The surviving degree-three structure is sharply restricted to Gallai trees.
not_killed: A polynomial contraction of degree-three Gallai-tree boundary gadgets into constraints on the degree-four core.
A direct invariant on pure 4-regular cores.
Hamiltonian/interlacement-specific contractions on the frozen hard source.

next_target.name: E8_GALLAI_TREE_BOUNDARY_GADGET_ELIMINATION_OR_4REG_CORE_V6_5
next_target.directive: After v6.4, either compile each remaining degree-three Gallai-tree component into a polynomial-size exact relation on its degree-four boundary and prove that the resulting global system is tractable, or return immediately to the pure 4-regular Hamiltonian source where the degree-three layer is empty. Reject any compilation whose boundary table is exponential in the number of attachments.

sources: P. Erdos, A. L. Rubin, H. Taylor, Choosability in graphs, 1979.
Modern restatement: a connected graph is degree-choosable iff it is not a Gallai tree.
